analysis.title: Microsoft: Broadening AI Momentum Builds
key_insights: MSFT F1Q revenue growth accelerated to 19% y/y @cc. Azure grew +48% @cc vs +44-45% guidance. M365 Commercial Cloud grew +18% @cc (19% adj.) vs +17% guidance. DB reiterates Buy.

Azure outperformance was driven by Foundry and improved CPU monetization, where engineering work unlocked additional GPU and CPU capacity. Higher revenue per token also helped, which DB understands can be episodic and tied to model-release cadence.
F2Q Azure guidance of +49%-50% @cc implies further acceleration despite third-party (3P) GPU capacity shifting into F2H. Demand still exceeds supply.

M365 Commercial Cloud outperformance came from stronger GitHub Copilot adoption and usage, plus premium Copilot, E5 and E7 SKUs. Weaker M365 E3 and standalone SKU execution weighed on commercial seat growth. F2Q is guided to +19% y/y @cc, with further acceleration expected through FY27, largely from ARPU.

CapEx of $45bn was below expectations because of 3P capacity delays, and 3/4ths of it went to short-lived assets. F2Q CapEx is guided to the >$50bn range, bringing calendar-year CapEx to ~$170bn. F2H CapEx steps up on CPUs (including higher memory and storage costs), GPUs and the delayed 3P capacity.

Operating margin came in ~1pt ahead of guidance and expanded 1pt y/y. Agents & Infra gross margin improved q/q, with y/y compression easing. Devices & Consumer gross margin expanded ~2pts y/y, helped by lower Activision-related intangible amortization.
F2Q gross/operating margins are guided to 66%/46.8% at the midpoint, down 1pt/0.3pts y/y. DB sees Microsoft set up well for the full-year guide of an operating margin decline of less than 1pt y/y.
Management reiterated Microsoft will remain FCF positive in FY27 despite accelerating F2H CapEx, and expects to access additional funding when attractive.

From the callback: DB says Azure's recent beat cadence may be hard to extrapolate into F2Q. The F1Q revenue-per-token benefit may not repeat, and 3P GPU capacity that would have supported in-period revenue shifted to F2H, leaving less room for upside to the guide.

AI infrastructure investment is supply constrained (powered shells), not capital or ROI constrained. Microsoft would deploy more capital if more powered shells were available, and FCF is an output of the model rather than a cap on spending.
Reliance on 3P capacity adds execution and timing risk and more quarterly variability in CapEx, available supply and Azure growth.

In Industry Solutions, CRM and HCM customers are evaluating how AI-enabled offerings may reshape application workflows before committing, which extends deal cycles and sometimes causes pauses. ERP booking trends remain relatively resilient.

market_movers.rationale: Azure and M365 Commercial Cloud sustain durable growth, AI monetization is broadening, and operating leverage offsets elevated investment. Stock closed at $531.01 on 28 Oct 26.

sector_views.rationale: DB is positive on Microsoft as AI adoption and monetization broaden across the stack. Separately, CRM and HCM application customers are pausing some deals to assess AI-enabled offerings.

earnings_insights: MSFT F1Q (reported, quarter ended September 2026): revenue growth +19% y/y @cc, accelerated from prior quarter. Azure +48% @cc reported vs +44-45% company guidance. M365 Commercial Cloud +18% @cc reported (+19% adj.) vs +17% company guidance.
MSFT F1Q CapEx (reported) was $45bn, below expectations due to 3P capacity delays. 3/4ths of it went to short-lived assets.
MSFT F1Q operating margin (reported) was ~1pt above company guidance and up 1pt y/y.

MSFT F2Q guidance (company, not yet reported): Azure +49%-50% @cc, M365 Commercial Cloud +19% y/y @cc, CapEx >$50bn, gross margin 66% and operating margin 46.8% at the midpoint (down 1pt and 0.3pts y/y).
MSFT calendar-year CapEx is guided to ~$170bn. Management guides full-year operating margin down less than 1pt y/y and FCF positive in FY27.
risk_factors: 3P capacity delivery timing is less in Microsoft's control, creating variability in CapEx, supply and Azure growth.
Revenue-per-token benefit in Azure may not repeat because it depends on model mix and release cadence.
Weak M365 E3 and standalone SKU execution weighed on commercial seat growth.
AI-enabled application offerings are extending deal cycles and causing some pauses in CRM and HCM within Industry Solutions.
Rising memory and storage costs add to CapEx.

tension_points.bull_case: Azure grew +48% @cc vs +44-45% guidance, F2Q is guided to +49%-50%, and demand exceeds supply, with efficiency gains unlocking more GPU and CPU capacity.
tension_points.bear_case: The F1Q revenue-per-token benefit can be episodic, and 3P GPU capacity shifted into F2H, leaving less room for upside to the F2Q guide.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An Azure F2Q result that does not exceed the +49%-50% @cc guide, which would show the beat cadence has stalled.
